claims.text: From 2026-10-30 Pro 200 ChatGPT Work and Codex usage drops from 20x to 10x Plus; GPT-6 Pro chat from 200 to 100 messages/week; price unchanged; current limits kept through 2026-10-29.
Existing Pro 200 subscribers get a one-time 62,500 usage credits (US$2,500) expiring 2026-12-31.
claims.notes: Whether credits require an active subscription is not stated in the email.

claims.text: OpenAI commits not to bring back the 5-hour usage limit.
Tibo: the new calculation nets out at half the dollar in API spend compared with the old Pro $200 plan.
claims.notes: Wording from the post as rendered in search results.

claims.text: Pro 500 costs $500/month with 25x Plus usage and is the only Pro tier with Ultrafast (up to 300 tokens/s in Codex).
Plus (1x/$20), Pro 100 (5x/$100), new Pro 200 (10x/$200) and Pro 500 (25x/$500) all price usage at $20 per 1x; the old Pro 200 (20x/$200) was the only volume discount.
claims.notes: Arithmetic on published multipliers; Pro 100 multiplier from OpenAI help pages as reported.

claims.text: GPT-6.1 Sol API: $2 input, $0.10 cached input, $10 output per 1M tokens; GPT-6 Astra: $10, $1.00, $50.
Claude Opus 5.5 cache hits cost 0.05x input ($0.20/M); Fable 5.1 cache hits 0.025x ($0.25/M); other Claude models 0.1x.
Aaron's 30 days (2026-08-31..09-29) on one Mac price at about $9,400 of Claude Code usage and about $3,900 of Codex usage at API list rates.
claims.notes: Lower bound for Codex; subscription tier on Claude is Max (tier not verified locally).

claims.text: Cache reads are 58-77% of the priced cost for each main model in Aaron's agentic coding usage.
The same Astra tokens priced at GPT-6.1 Sol cost about 12% as much ($3,105 vs $383).
claims.notes: Price comparison only; does not establish Sol can do the same work.

claims.text: In September, Aaron's Pro account weekly Codex meter reached 99-100% in five windows; a second Pro 100 account reached 95-96%.

Community reaction concentrated on timing and framing (cut announced the night before DevDay; 'just say you're cutting limits in half'), on switching to Claude, and on a minority view that the math is less bad than claimed.
claims.notes: Reddit not collected (SSL failure); <48h of reaction; low engagement on most X posts.

claims.text: Aaron forecasts that coding subscriptions will increasingly be expressed as visible API-dollar budgets and that price competition moves to cache-read and speed tiers.
claims.notes: Forecast; label as Aaron's inference in copy.
